parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
In aqueous solution, persulfate ions, $\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}$, react with iodide ions, as shown in reaction 1.

reaction 1 $$\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-} + 2\text{I}^- \rightarrow 2\text{SO}_4^{2-} + \text{I}_2$$

The rate of reaction 1 is investigated.

A sample of $\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}$ is mixed with a large excess of iodide ions of known concentration. The graph in Fig. 5.1 shows the results obtained.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Fig. 5.1
parts.text: Use Fig. 5.1 to determine the initial rate of reaction 1. Show your working.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
The rate equation for reaction 1 is $\text{rate} = k [\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}][\text{I}^-]$.

Suggest why a large excess of iodide ions allows the rate constant to be determined from the half-life in this investigation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The reaction of persulfate ions, $\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}$, with iodide ions is catalysed by $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ ions.

Write **two** equations to show how $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ catalyses reaction 1.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Describe the effect of an increase in temperature on the rate constant and the rate of reaction 1.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
In aqueous solution, thiosulfate ions, $\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}$, react with hydrogen ions, as shown in reaction 2.

reaction 2 $$\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} + 2\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{SO}_2 + \text{S} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

The rate of reaction is first order with respect to $[\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}]$ and zero order with respect to $[\text{H}^+]$ under certain conditions.

The rate constant, $k$, for this reaction is $1.58 \times 10^{-2}\text{s}^{-1}$.

Calculate the half-life, $t_{\frac{1}{2}}$, for reaction 2.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
The compound nitrosyl bromide, $\text{NOBr}$, can be formed as shown in reaction 3.

reaction 3 $$2\text{NO}(\text{g}) + \text{Br}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{NOBr}(\text{g})$$

The rate is first order with respect to $[\text{NO}]$ and first order with respect to $[\text{Br}_2]$.

The reaction mechanism has two steps.

Suggest equations for the **two** steps of this mechanism. State which is the rate-determining step.
